Trigger or failure mode: Synthetic source evidence is linked despite missing, conflicting or unverified Patient or Encounter references
Worst credible workflow effect: Evidence or an attributable action is associated with the wrong episode and later work may be misdirected
Potential harm scope: One episode per occurrence; potentially broader if a shared linkage rule is defective
Immediacy: Immediate once attachment or downstream reliance occurs
Reversibility: Partially reversible: the internal reference and history can be corrected, but prior human reliance cannot be assumed undone
Preventive controls: Verify Patient, Encounter and event references before attachment; quarantine uncertainty; prohibit autonomous matching
Detection evidence: Fixture reconciliation, blocked-linkage test, exception evidence and audit review
Recovery or containment: Preserve the last verified state, route to `Patient Match Failed` or `Encounter Missing`, require Identity reconciliation reviewer evidence and append correction/recovery history
Accountable owner: Product owner; Identity reconciliation reviewer resolves the case
Related requirements and controls: AP-03; FR-03; NFR-03; SCR-07; EVT-04; EVT-19; EVT-21
Planned scenario or test: PS-02; UAT-FR-03; linked SIT and recovery test
Release response: No-Go while unsafe attachment or silent progression remains possible
Residual uncertainty: Real participant identifiers, matching policy, MPI behaviour and error prevalence are untested
Evidence status: Executed synthetic evidence: T-QLT-601-01/02 and T-QLT-601-03 covered missing-encounter quarantine, no attachment/state advance and accountable exception recovery. No real identity matching or harm claim.

Hazard: Superseded or wrong report version used
Trigger or failure mode: A revised DiagnosticReport arrives but review, AI draft, direction or handoff continues using an earlier version
Worst credible workflow effect: Human review or downstream handling relies on stale diagnostic evidence
Potential harm scope: One episode per occurrence; potentially broader if version-control logic is defective
Immediacy: Immediate at the next review or action; latent while stale evidence remains unnoticed
Reversibility: Partially reversible: review can reopen and evidence can be superseded, but downstream reliance requires human reassessment
Preventive controls: Require current source version, preserve prior acknowledgement as history, mark dependent drafts/evidence stale and block unreviewed progression
Detection evidence: Amended-result scenario, source-version comparison, stale-output control and audit trace
Recovery or containment: Return to `Clinical Review Pending`, require renewed clinician review and reassessment, and append supersession/correction evidence
Accountable owner: Product owner; Clinic physician owns renewed review
Related requirements and controls: AP-05; FR-25; FR-32; SCR-03; SCR-08; EVT-08; EVT-10; EVT-20
Release response: No-Go when stale evidence remains actionable or renewed review can be bypassed
Residual uncertainty: Source-specific amendment policy and real report-version behaviour require participant validation
Evidence status: Executed synthetic evidence: T-QLT-601-01/02 checked current-version and amended-report re-review; AI-EVAL-QLT-603-02 blocked stale acceptance and returned to SCR-03. No real source-version policy claim.

Trigger or failure mode: A role, deterministic rule or simulated AI output records acknowledgement, direction, referral response, financial decision or closure without the required human authority
Worst credible workflow effect: A consequential workflow decision is attributed incorrectly or the episode progresses without accountable approval
Potential harm scope: Any episode using the affected control; potentially all gated actions if the permission rule is shared
Immediacy: Immediate when the unauthorised action changes workflow evidence or state
Reversibility: Not fully reversible: state and audit can be corrected, but an external or human response cannot be assumed undone
Preventive controls: Role-based visibility, explicit confirmation, separate human decision events and no direct AI state effect
Detection evidence: Permission tests, actor/role audit evidence, attempted-action logs and unsafe-autonomous-action metric
Recovery or containment: Block the action, preserve attempted-action evidence, restore the last verified state and require the authorised human decision
Accountable owner: Product owner; authorised decision owner for the affected gate
Related requirements and controls: AP-06; AP-08; NFR-05; NFR-08; SCR-03 to SCR-06; SCR-10
Release response: No-Go for any unresolved authority bypass or unsafe autonomous action
Residual uncertainty: Production identity, session security and organisational role assignment remain untested
Evidence status: Executed synthetic evidence: T-QLT-601-01 and T-QLT-601-03 exercised role-gated acknowledgement, direction, routing, receiving response, confirmation, closure and recovery; T-QLT-603-01 retained no AI state effect. No production identity claim.

Hazard: Unsupported, omitted or prohibited AI content accepted
Trigger or failure mode: A pre-written AI fixture contains a material unsupported statement, critical omission, wrong-patient/version reference or prohibited recommendation and is treated as usable
Worst credible workflow effect: A reviewer may rely on misleading workflow or handoff content
Potential harm scope: One reviewed output per occurrence; potentially broader if the same control failure affects an output type
Immediacy: Immediate when relied upon; latent when an omission or stale reference is not noticed
Reversibility: Reversible before reliance through rejection; partially reversible after operational use because human reassessment is required
Preventive controls: Source links and versions, visible uncertainty, output-type checklist, canonical human disposition, stale-output control and no direct state effect
Detection evidence: Output-level rubric review, unsupported/omission annotation, reviewer disposition and AI audit evidence
Recovery or containment: Reject, correct, discard or supersede the output; preserve the complete manual workflow and record fallback
Accountable owner: Product owner; designated clinical or operational reviewer
Related requirements and controls: AI-01; AI-02; FR-15; FR-16; SCR-08; EVT-20; AI evaluation rubric
Planned scenario or test: AI wrong-patient, stale-version, unsupported-content, omission and forced-unavailable cases
Release response: Defer the affected assist or record No-Go if the core workflow cannot continue safely
Residual uncertainty: The prototype uses pre-written outputs and cannot establish deployed-model safety or general performance
Evidence status: QLT-603 fixture-level evidence recorded: current, stale and represented-unavailable controls passed with manual fallback. Unsupported and omission prevalence remains unevaluated because no unsafe content fixture exists; no deployed-model or clinical-safety claim.

Hazard: Failed action shown as success or duplicate progression
Trigger or failure mode: A denied write, unavailable service, retry or replay is displayed as completed or advances the episode twice
Worst credible workflow effect: Users act on false workflow evidence, ownership or completion status
Potential harm scope: One episode per occurrence; potentially broader if shared retry/idempotency logic is defective
Immediacy: Immediate when false success is displayed or duplicate state change occurs
Reversibility: Partially reversible through linked correction and recovery; external reliance cannot be assumed undone
Preventive controls: Explicit pending/failed states, stable idempotency keys, last-verified-state recovery and prohibition on treating failure as success
Detection evidence: Failure/retry tests, duplicate-event evidence, state-before/after comparison and audit reconciliation
Recovery or containment: Keep the failure visible, prevent duplicate advancement, return to the last verified state and reprocess only verified evidence
Accountable owner: Product owner; Product/platform administrator owns technical recovery
Related requirements and controls: AP-09; AP-10; NFR-03; NFR-06; SCR-07; SCR-09; EVT-19; EVT-21
Planned scenario or test: PS-02; PS-03; PS-04; linked SIT retry/recovery test
Release response: No-Go while false success, duplicate advancement or unrecoverable failure remains possible
Residual uncertainty: Production transport guarantees, concurrency and external-system recovery are not tested
Evidence status: Executed synthetic evidence: T-QLT-601-01/02 covered unavailable access, duplicate evidence without second state advance, safe-return recovery and no false-success behaviour. No transport/concurrency claim.

Trigger or failure mode: Sent or delivered communication evidence is promoted to patient understanding, acceptance or next-step confirmation without the required evidence
Worst credible workflow effect: The diagnostic-closure workflow may appear complete while the accountable next step remains unconfirmed
Potential harm scope: One episode per occurrence; potentially broader if closure logic uses delivery as a universal proxy
Immediacy: Latent until the missing confirmation affects follow-up or closure review
Reversibility: Partially reversible: the episode can reopen or remain pending, but elapsed time and missed follow-up cannot be recovered
Preventive controls: Keep preparation, approval, sending, delivery and explicit confirmation separate; require pathway-specific closure evidence
Detection evidence: Closure checklist, communication-event comparison, blocked-confirmation test and audit review
Recovery or containment: Keep the workflow pending or route the missing evidence to visible owned work; record confirmation only from approved evidence
Accountable owner: Product owner; Care Coordinator verifies closure evidence
Release response: Change and retest; No-Go if false closure remains possible
Residual uncertainty: Real communication channels, patient understanding and confirmation policy are not validated
Evidence status: Executed synthetic evidence: T-QLT-601-01 and T-QLT-601-03 required separate evidence-gated next-step confirmation and later scoped closure. No real communication or participant-understanding claim.

Hazard: Referral handoff remains unowned or is mistaken for acceptance
Trigger or failure mode: Package preparation or sending is treated as receiving-team acceptance, or no accountable owner is visible while response is pending
Worst credible workflow effect: Follow-up responsibility is unclear and the next safe step may remain unresolved
Potential harm scope: One referral or escalation episode per occurrence; potentially multiple episodes if assignment or response logic is defective
Immediacy: Latent and increases with unresolved ageing; immediate when the workflow falsely records acceptance
Reversibility: Usually reversible when detected before downstream reliance; elapsed coordination time cannot be recovered
Preventive controls: Separate preparation, routing, receiving response and next-step confirmation; require named owner, destination, timeframe and response evidence
Detection evidence: Owner/ageing review, handoff-state tests, receiving-response evidence and unresolved-handoff metric
Recovery or containment: Keep the referral pending, assign accountable work, record rejection or response accurately and require confirmation evidence
Accountable owner: Product owner; Referral Coordinator and receiving team retain their distinct responsibilities
Related requirements and controls: FR-09; FR-10; FR-11; FR-24; SCR-05; SCR-06; SCR-10; EVT-12; EVT-13; EVT-14; EVT-16
Planned scenario or test: PS-01; UAT-FR-10; UAT-FR-11; handoff ownership test
Release response: Change and retest; No-Go if sent work can be represented as accepted or confirmed
Residual uncertainty: Real referral routing, response times and organisational ownership remain unvalidated
Evidence status: Executed synthetic evidence: T-QLT-601-01 and T-QLT-601-03 kept package routing, receiving acceptance and next-step confirmation distinct with named owners. No live referral-routing claim.
